Block by block

Var(X₁) = σ² + σ² = 2σ²
Var(X₂) = 2σ² + 2σ² = 4σ²
Var(X₃) = 4σ² + 4σ² = 8σ²
Var(X₄) = 8σ² + 8σ² = 16σ²
Variance diverges to infinity
For a block with input variance σₓ²: Var(Ŷ) = f·(2/f)·σₓ² = 2σₓ² · E[P̂²] = ½·2σₓ² = σₓ²
Var(block out) = n·(1/n)·E[P̂²] = σₓ²
Var(Xₗ) = Var(Xₗ₋₁) + Var(block out) = 2·Var(Xₗ₋₁), so Var(Xₗ) = 2ˡσ²
With no control, the stream’s variance doubles every block and diverges.

Residual provides gradient identity path

Residual connections
Xₗ₊₁ = Xₗ + F(Xₗ)
F(Xₗ) = A(Xₗ Winᵀ) Woutᵀ
Variance of Xₗ directly passes through to next layer (no attenuation)
∂Xₗ₊₁/∂Xₗ = 1 + ∂Xₗ₊₁/∂Fₗ · ∂Fₗ/∂Xₗ
Gradient now has an identity path
∂L/∂Xₗ = ∂L/∂Xₗ₊₁ · ∂Xₗ₊₁/∂Xₗ
= ∂L/∂Xₗ₊₁ + ∂L/∂Xₗ₊₁ · ∂Xₗ₊₁/∂Fₗ · ∂Fₗ/∂Xₗ
Often ignore Wout. Purpose is to rescale output before residual. Important but doesn’t change the gradient or statistics.

Var(∂L/∂X₀) = 8σ² + 8σ² = 16σ²

Variance diverges to infinity
For a block whose incoming gradient ∂L/∂Xₗ has variance v: Var(∂L/∂P̂) = f·(1/n)·v = (f/n)v · Var(∂L/∂Ŷ) = ½·(f/n)v
Var(block out) = n·(2/f)·½(f/n)v = v
Var(∂L/∂Xₗ₋₁) = Var(∂L/∂Xₗ) + Var(block out) = 2·Var(∂L/∂Xₗ), so Var(∂L/∂X₀) = 2⁴σ²
The residual stream trades vanishing gradients for exploding ones.

Introduce a scaling factor

Multiply each block’s output by αₗ before it joins the stream
X₁
X₂ ⋯ Xₗ₋₁
General residual MLP
Xₗ = Xₗ₋₁ + αₗ · Fₗ(Xₗ₋₁)
Fₗ = · Wᵀ → ReLU → · Wᵀ with He init, so each block returns the variance it reads.
αₗ = 1/√L keeps the output variance below e·σ²
αₗ = 1/√l makes Var(Xₗ) = (l + 1)σ²
All of these configs can work. (a) and (b) are preferred.
A per-block factor αₗ controls how much variance each block adds.

Where the scaling factor goes

All of these configs can work. (a) and (b) are preferred.
(a) Scale the block input
Xₗ₋₁
Xₗ
Xₗ = Xₗ₋₁ + Fₗ(α·Xₗ₋₁)
Scale the variance going in:
block reads α²·Var(Xₗ₋₁)
and returns α²·Var(Xₗ₋₁)
stream adds α²·Var(Xₗ₋₁)
existing stream variance untouched
Same as (b)
(b) Scale the block output
Xₗ₋₁
Xₗ
Xₗ = Xₗ₋₁ + α·Fₗ(Xₗ₋₁)
Scale the variance coming out:
block reads Var(Xₗ₋₁)
and returns α²·Var(Xₗ₋₁)
stream adds α²·Var(Xₗ₋₁)
existing stream variance untouched
Same as (a)
(c) Scale the stream
Xₗ₋₁
Xₗ
Xₗ = α·Xₗ₋₁ + Fₗ(Xₗ₋₁)
Scale the stream’s variance:
stream keeps α²·Var(Xₗ₋₁)
block still adds Var(Xₗ₋₁)
Var(Xₗ) = (α² + 1)·Var(Xₗ₋₁)
X₀ and earlier blocks shrink by α²
Avoid
Scale the block, not the stream: (c) shrinks X₀ and every earlier block by α².
© 2026 Dr. Jesse Roberts

Scaling for convergence

Where should the shrinking factor go: on the whole stream, or only on each layer?
Two options
Attenuate the residual and layer
Xₗ₊₃ = αₗ₊₂(Xₗ₊₂ + F(Xₗ₊₂Wᵀ))
= αₗ₊₂(αₗ₊₁(αₗ(Xₗ + F(XₗWᵀ)) + F(Xₗ₊₁Wᵀ)) + F(Xₗ₊₂Wᵀ))
  • Scaling the residual stream shrinks the variance of X in the stream
  • Gradient identity path is now attenuated by scaling
Attenuate the layer
Xₗ₊₃ = Xₗ₊₂ + F(αₗ₊₂Xₗ₊₂Wᵀ)
= Xₗ + F(αₗXₗWᵀ) + F(αₗ₊₁Xₗ₊₁Wᵀ) + F(αₗ₊₂Xₗ₊₂Wᵀ)
αₗ₊₂ < αₗ₊₁ < αₗ
  • Variance of X is preserved
  • Gradient identity path is preserved
Attenuating the layer is preferred
  • Doesn’t attenuate the input Xₗ as a function of L
  • Preserves the identity path
Shrink each layer’s contribution, never the identity path.

Var(X₁) = σ² + 1·σ² = 2σ²
Var(X₂) = 2σ² + ½·2σ² = 3σ²

  • The variance grows like σ² ∗ 2L
    • What if we introduce a scaling to each layer
      • All layers multiplied by 1/√l
σ² ∏l=1L (1 + 1/l) = (L + 1)σ²
  • Early layers contribute more variance
Block l’s output is multiplied by 1/√l before the add, so the variance it adds is scaled by (1/√l)² = 1/l
For block input variance σₓ²: Var(Ŷ) = f·(2/f)·σₓ² = 2σₓ² · E[P̂²] = ½·2σₓ² = σₓ² · Var(block out) = n·(1/n)·σₓ² = σₓ²
Block l reads Var(Xₗ₋₁) = l·σ², so it adds (1/l)·l·σ² = σ²
so Var(Xₗ) = Var(Xₗ₋₁) + σ² = (l + 1)σ², growing linearly with depth
With 1/√l, variance grows linearly with depth instead of exponentially.

  • The variance grows like σ² ∗ 2L
    • What if we introduce a scaling to each layer
      • All layers multiplied by 1/√L
σ² (1 + 1/L)L < eσ²
  • All layers contribute equal variance
Each block’s output is multiplied by 1/√L before the add, so the variance it adds is scaled by (1/√L)² = 1/L = ¼
For block input variance σₓ²: Var(Ŷ) = f·(2/f)·σₓ² = 2σₓ² · E[P̂²] = ½·2σₓ² = σₓ² · Var(block out) = n·(1/n)·σₓ² = σₓ²
Var(Xₗ) = Var(Xₗ₋₁) + (1/L)·Var(Xₗ₋₁) = (1 + 1/L)·Var(Xₗ₋₁)
so Var(XL) = (1 + 1/L)L σ² = 2.44σ² for L = 4, and stays below eσ² ≈ 2.72σ² at any depth
With 1/√L, variance stays below eσ² at any depth.

For each feature j:
μⱼ = mean of column j
σⱼ² = variance of column j
X̂ᵢⱼ = (Xᵢⱼ − μⱼ) / √(σⱼ² + ε)
Yᵢⱼ = γⱼX̂ᵢⱼ + βⱼ
γⱼ = 1, βⱼ = 0 at init (learned)
at inference: running μⱼ, σⱼ²
ε prevents amplifying noise too much.
In model.train() mode, stats come from batch.
In model.eval() mode, stats come from the most recent window of inputs.

σᵢ² = variance of row i
X̂ᵢⱼ = (Xᵢⱼ − μᵢ) / √(σᵢ² + ε)
Yᵢⱼ = γⱼX̂ᵢⱼ + βⱼ
γⱼ = 1, βⱼ = 0 at init (per feature)
same at training and inference
ε prevents amplifying noise too much.
Stats are always based on the current vector across features.
One example’s features through the steps
Input row Xᵢ
mean μᵢ, var σᵢ²
1 · subtract μᵢ
mean 0, var σᵢ²
2 · divide by √(σᵢ² + ε)
mean 0, var 1
3 · scale γⱼ, shift βⱼ
mean 0, var 1 at init
LayerNorm standardizes each example across its features, the same at training and inference.

Each norm scales the variance to 1.
For early layers the scaling is near 1.
For later layers the scaling is near 1/√l.
Similar to scaling by 1/√l.
Early layers contribute more!
Norm (BatchNorm or LayerNorm, γ = 1 and β = 0 at init) rescales whatever variance the stream has to 1
Var(Ŷ) = f·(2/f)·1 = 2 · E[P̂²] = ½·2 = 1 · Var(block out) = n·(1/n)·1 = 1
every block adds exactly 1: Var(Xₗ) = Var(Xₗ₋₁) + 1
so Var(Xₗ) = σ² + l, linear growth with no hand-picked multiplier
With a norm in front of every block, Var(Xₗ) = σ² + l, no multiplier to pick.

Norm (BatchNorm or LayerNorm, γ = 1 and β = 0 at init) rescales whatever variance the stream has to 1
Var(Ŷ) = f·(2/f)·1 = 2 · E[P̂²] = ½·2 = 1 · Var(block out) = n·(1/n)·1 = 1
every block adds exactly 1: Var(Xₗ) = Var(Xₗ₋₁) + 1, so Var(Xₗ) = σ² + l
The stream is never normalized (X₄ still has σ²+4); the final norm branches off it, just like each block’s norm, so the output leaving the network has variance 1
A final norm hands the next layer an input with variance 1.

Final norm for scaling

We end as if the network’s output is the input to another layer
The final norm rescales the output without touching the stream.
